blurb: A contract clause is checked on every call in the dev and test build, and by the runner on generated inputs, so its predicate must be a pure `Bool` over the parameters and `result`. Effects (`Effect.pure`, `?`) and test-only constructs (`expect`, `val`, observations, `faults`, `trace`) cannot appear in it. State the claim as a plain comparison, and keep assertions and effects in a `case`.
example:
fn inc(x: Int) -> Int
  ensures bigger: expect result > x   // ✗ `expect` is a test statement

fn inc(x: Int) -> Int
  ensures bigger: result > x          // ✓ a pure `Bool`
summary: A contract predicate uses an effectful or test-only construct; a contract clause must be pure.
